questions.question: On a freeway, you missed your turn or exit. What should you do?

options.text: Make the turn quickly from your current lane.
Stop and back up.
Keep driving until you find the next exit or safe place to turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving until you find the next exit or safe place to turn around.
questions.explanation: If you miss your turn or exit, do not back up. Continue to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around. It is illegal to back up on a freeway shoulder.

questions.question: Which safety restraints work best in a crash?

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Only an airbag.
Both a lap and shoulder belt and an airbag.
No safety restraints.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap and shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts double your chance of surviving a crash and greatly reduce serious injuries. Airbags work best when used with safety belts during a front-end crash. Always wear both your shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: How can you reduce fatigue on a long drive?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Do arm exercises every hour.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Switch which foot you use on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Take a break every two hours on long trips to avoid fatigue. If you feel drowsy, pull over to a safe place and nap or rest for the night.

questions.question: How can you make sure your physical condition does not affect your safe driving?

options.text: Stay physically fit and have regular medical check-ups.
Know how any medicine you take affects your driving.
Drive within your physical limits.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Your physical condition is important for safe driving. Know your physical limits and only drive when it is safe for you to do so.

questions.question: What should you do if you are in a serious car crash?

options.text: Stop.
Call the police.
Check if anyone is hurt.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: In a crash, move your vehicle off the road and stop if possible. If anyone is hurt, call 911 and help them. You must report the crash to police if someone is injured, someone is killed, or damage is more than $1,000 (or more than $200 to government property like signs).

questions.question: Your car breaks down on a highway. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your hazard flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your hazard flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: If your car breaks down on the highway, signal and carefully exit the roadway. Turn on your hazard flashers. Park as far off the road as possible where other drivers can see you. Raise your hood to show your car is disabled.

questions.question: One of your tires blows out while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Brake hard right away.
Keep the steering wheel straight and slowly take your foot off the gas pedal.
Keep driving at the same speed and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to alert drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the steering wheel straight and slowly take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows, hold the steering wheel tight and keep the car straight. Ease off the gas pedal. Do not brake until you have full control. Once the car is steady, brake gently and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than any train nearby.
Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
Look for a way to drive around any lowered gates.
Assume no trains are coming and drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs alert you that a train may be near. Always obey these signs. Never go around barriers or ignore the warning.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Stop where you are.
Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle behind you, make space for it and stop. Slow down and safely pull to the side of the road. If you are in heavy traffic and the emergency vehicle is directly behind you, move slowly until you can get out of its way.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection. Pedestrians are crossing against the red light. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Speed up and drive in front of the pedestrians.
Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to the pedestrians to scare them so they do not cross against red lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians, even if you have a green light. Be careful around pedestrians in every situation.

questions.question: Smoking and preparing to smoke while driving:

options.text: Do not affect driving abilities.
Help keep drivers alert.
Are distracting activities.
Are not distracting activities.

questions.explanation: Smoking while driving distracts you. You may take your hands off the wheel or your eyes off the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No passing zone.
Winding road.
Pedestrian crossing.
Low ground railroad crossing.

questions.explanation: This sign warns of a low ground railroad crossing. The railroad tracks cross the road at a steep slope. Low vehicles may drag or get stuck on the tracks.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks are permitted on an upcoming narrow bridge.
The bridge ahead is open to one-way traffic only.
The bridge ahead is wide enough for only one car at a time.
The bridge ahead may be too narrow to meet or pass a truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The bridge ahead may be too narrow to meet or pass a truck.
questions.explanation: This warning sign tells drivers that an upcoming bridge may be too narrow to meet or pass a truck. Drive carefully and be prepared.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Don't drink if you are going to drive.
Slippery when wet.
Road curves ahead.
You are approaching a hill.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. Signals tell other drivers what you plan to do and help prevent accidents.

questions.question: When you see other drivers acting or reacting in anger:

options.text: Don't make eye contact.
Don't react with hand gestures.
Distance yourself from the situation.
All of these.

questions.explanation: When other drivers are angry, stay away from them. Avoid eye contact and don't make gestures that might upset them. Slow down, move over, or do whatever you safely can to avoid danger.

questions.question: When approaching a red traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Drive through the intersection if there is no crossing traffic.
Continue driving, as they have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.explanation: A red traffic light means you must stop completely. Driving through a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red only if there is no sign that prohibits it.

questions.question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, the driver must show:

options.text: Proof of insurance.
Their license.
Proof of registration.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When stopped, you must show your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance. You must carry all three documents when driving.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, you should:

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach you.
Get out of your car and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach you.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel and ask passengers to keep their hands visible. Stay in your car unless the officer asks you to exit. Wait for the officer to ask for your license, registration, and insurance.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Get some coffee.
Open your window.
Stop driving.
Turn on the radio.

questions.explanation: Driving while tired is as dangerous as driving drunk. If you feel tired, stop driving.

questions.question: What is the purpose of highway markings?

options.text: They are not very important.
They only appear in construction zones.
They give drivers information.
They are usually red and blue.

questions.explanation: Highway markings give drivers information. They help drivers stay in the correct lane, show safe passing areas, and warn about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Stop right away.
Help injured people.
Call the police.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: If you have an accident, stop your vehicle immediately. If you can, move it out of traffic. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people unnecessarily, but try to stop heavy bleeding by applying pressure. Wait for emergency help to arrive.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Exercise.
Wait for your body to break down the alcohol.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to break down the alcohol.
questions.explanation: The only way to lower your BAC is to not drink and wait for time to pass. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot lower your BAC or reduce alcohol's effects. They may help you stay awake, but they do not change your BAC or make you sober.

questions.question: How can you best avoid hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition.
Drive slower on wet or slushy roads.
Watch for standing water and puddles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: On wet roads, cars need more space to stop and may skid when turning quickly. Do not use cruise control in wet or icy conditions. Reduce your speed and drive carefully.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?

options.text: It improves driving skills but hurts judgment.
It hurts both driving skills and judgment.
It does not affect either driving skills or judgment.
It does not affect judgment but hurts driving skills.

questions.correctAnswerText: It hurts both driving skills and judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol harms many skills needed for safe driving, including your reaction time and eyesight. It also affects your ability to judge speed and distance, makes you less careful, and causes you to take more risks.
